sentences.text: Aggrieved by the award passed in MVC.No.477/2017 dated 02.07.2019 by the VIII Additional Small Causes Judge and the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (SCCH-5), Bengaluru whereby the Tribunal had granted an amount of Rs.11,30,000/- as compensation.
The insurance company as well as the claimants are before this Court.
2. The Insurance Company's appeal is MFA.No.8815/2019 and the claimant's appeal is MFA.No.1582/2020.
3. The claim petition is filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.40,00,000/- for the death of the deceased.

It is the case of the claimants that on 17.11.2016 at about 04.00 p.m. when the deceased was proceeding by riding the motorcycle and when he reached in front of Poultry Farrm of Mundy Sahadeva Naik near Kollafarm village, on Chittor Main Road, at that point of time, one auto driven by its driver in the rash and negligent manner endangering human life came on NC:
2025:KHC:34821 HC-KAR the wrong side with high speed and due to excessive speed the driver of the auto lost control over his vehicle and dashed against the motorcycle which resulted in the accident and the deceased had sustained injuries and succumbed to the same.
4. The Insurance Company before the Tribunal as well before this Court has raised two grounds.
Firstly, the driver of the offending auto is not having a LMV non transport.

Secondly, the policy is issued in the name of the dead person and that is obtained by playing fraud which they came to know after receiving the summons and as such they are not liable to pay the compensation.

5. The Tribunal had held that the driver is having a driving licence to drive the LMV non transport and relying on the judgment of Jagdish Kumar Sood Vs. United Insurance Co., Ltd and others1, the Tribunal had negatived the said contention of the Insurance Company.

entities.text: Jagdish Kumar Sood Vs. United Insurance Co., Ltd and others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Coming to the next contention with regard to the fake policy that is issued in the name of a dead person, the Tribunal held that before issuing policy the Insurance Company shall verify the document 2018 (3) SCC 697 NC: 2025:KHC:34821 HC-KAR pertaining to the vehicle and also a proposal form.

They have not lodged any complaint with regard to obtaining any policy by misrepresentation and those contentions cannot be taken and accordingly held that the Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation and awarded the compensation as per the table given below:

sentences.text: Learned counsel appearing for the claimant submits that that the Tribunal had considered Rs.7,000/- as a income.
But the Tribunal ought to have taken Rs.9,500/- as the income and even under other conventional heads also, the compensation that is awarded by the tribunal is not just reasonable.
NC: 2025:KHC:34821 HC-KAR 7.
Learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company has reiterated the grounds that were taken before the Tribunal and submits that the principle of pay and recovery will apply.
8. Having heard learned counsels on either side, perused the materials on record.

The two contentions that were raised by the Insurance Company with regard to the LMV license transport non-transport, that issue is no more res-integra as the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan Vs- Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.,2 held that still the Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan Vs- Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Then coming to the second ground regarding fake driving license, the Tribunal had rightly considered and passed an order and this Court is not inclined to interfere.
Coming to the enhancement of the compensation as the accident had occurred in the year 2016 the income has to be taken at Rs.9,500/-.
The deceased is aged 41 years, future prospects at 25% would come to Rs.2,375/- which comes to Rs.11,875/- (Rs.9,500+Rs.2,375).
As there are three dependents 1/3rd has to be deducted towards the personal expenses.
If the same is deducted, his (2017) 14 SCC 663 NC: 2025:KHC:34821 HC-KAR contribution to the family would be Rs.7,916/- per month.

Hence,
under the head of loss of dependency this court is granting an amount of Rs.13,29,888/-
(Rs.7,916x12x14).
As there are three claimants, towards loss of consortium an amount of Rs.1,32,000/- (Rs.44,000x3) is granted.
Towards funeral expenses, this Court is granting an amount of Rs.36,000/-.

9. In the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of V.Mekala vs. M.
Malathi and Another3, the claimant is entitled for an amount of Rs.10,000/- towards legal expenses.
